SUP-s109-supp xe:RAND:0:5:w17 step 31 (pass), xe:RAND:1:9:w10 step 21, w11 step 16, w12 step 25, w14 step 25, w15 step 21, w16 step 21 and xe:RAND:2:11:w18 step 33: gorge [] vs xmage [ability:Laboratory Drudge@p0] (some windows p1); Forge agrees with gorge (both suppress). Oracle text: "At the beginning of each end step, draw a card if you've cast a spell from a graveyard or activated an ability of a card in a graveyard this turn." The "if" follows the effect, not the trigger condition, so CR 603.4 does not make it an intervening-if: "A triggered ability may read 'When/Whenever/At [trigger event], if [condition], [effect].' When the trigger event occurs, the ability checks whether the stated condition is true. The ability triggers only if it is; otherwise it does nothing. ... This rule is referred to as the 'intervening if clause' rule. (The word 'if' has only its normal English meaning anywhere else in the text of a card; this rule only applies to an 'if' that immediately follows a trigger condition.)" The 2020-11-10 ruling: "Laboratory Drudge's ability will trigger at the beginning of each end step whether you've cast a spell from a graveyard or activated an ability of a card in a graveyard that turn or not." The ability must trigger every end step and check the condition at resolution; XMage's ConditionalOneShotEffect on LaboratoryDrudge.java:32-37 (condition at resolution) is correct. Gorge and Forge are wrong: .cards/cardsfolder/l/laboratory_drudge.txt:5 puts CheckSVar$ NumCast on the T:Mode$ Phase line, and gorge engine/rules/trigger_condition.go:423-461 reads CheckSVar as an intervening-if. evidence: blame|GF|X|stack|High Stride. BLB-s343-rand xe:RAND:0:11:w5 at step 20 (cast): gorge [ability:Nettle Guard@p0, spell:High Stride@p0] vs xmage [spell:High Stride@p0]; class 3way:GF|X, forge=agree, xmage=diverge. The spell is not the defect: it is the cast that targets a Valiant creature (Nettle Guard / Flowerfoot Swordmaster) whose Valiant trigger gorge and Forge put on the stack and XMage does not. Valiant (BLB): 'Whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability you control for the first time each turn, ...'. CR 603.2: 'Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers.' The trigger event is a targeting by a spell or ability its controller controls, so a targeting by the opponent's spell earlier in the turn is not an occurrence of that event and does not use up 'the first time' (CR 207.2c: an ability word has no rules meaning of its own; the card text decides). XMage counts every targeting: BecomesTargetSourceFirstTimeTriggeredAbility.checkTrigger (Mage/src/main/java/mage/abilities/common/BecomesTargetSourceFirstTimeTriggeredAbility.java:36) rejects when NumberOfTimesPermanentTargetedATurnWatcher.numTimesTargetedThisTurn (Mage/src/main/java/mage/watchers/common/NumberOfTimesPermanentTargetedATurnWatcher.java:43) is above 1, and the watcher increments for every TARGETED event whatever the targeting object's controller, while ValiantTriggeredAbility only filters the current targeting by 'you'. Corroborating engines: Forge Card.isValiant (forge-game/src/main/java/forge/game/card/Card.java:3681: getController().equals(p) && !targetedFromThisTurn.contains(p), recorded per targeting player at MagicStack.java:423-426) and gorge trigmatch valiantFirstTimeTargetedByYouThisTurn (engine/rules/trigmatch/actions.go:485, selected by Valiant$ at actions.go:291) both count only the controller's own targetings. In the window a spell of the opponent (p0's Might of the Meek on the stack under the cast, or an earlier opposing High Stride/pump) had already targeted the Valiant creature this turn, which is the only way XMage's count reaches 2 with the controller's first own targeting; the repro directory was pruned from the farm box before this seat read it, so the earlier targeting is inferred from the stack at the cast checkpoint and the Forge/gorge agreement, and the mechanism is proved by the fork test instead of a replay. Failing-first fork test ValiantFirstTimeTest.testOpponentTargetingFirstDoesNotUseUpValiant (Nettle Guard 3/1; the opponent's High Stride at upkeep, then the controller's own High Stride in main phase): on the prebuilt mage 1.4.63 jars (xmageoracle-trek, ref 4142596) it fails with 'no such creature ... with specified p/t of 5/9 ... power=5 toughness=7' and passes with the patch; the control testSecondOwnTargetingDoesNotTriggerValiant (the controller's own second targeting still does not trigger) passes both (JUnitCore, 2 tests). Fix: the watcher records the targeting controller and ValiantTriggeredAbility counts only its controller's targetings through a protected hook; Glyph Keeper, Angelic Cub and the other users of the generic class keep the all-targetings count their text asks for. Verdict (b) XMage; no gorge change.

evidence: blame|GF|X|stack|Grand Nagus Zek. 3 farm windows, class 3way:GF|X with xmage=diverge (forge=agree) and the twin xmage:diverge:stack row: TRK-s240-rand xe:RAND:4:19:w15 (gorge [] vs xmage [ability:Grand Nagus Zek@p1] @ step 23 (pass)); TRK-s370-rand xe:RAND:2:16:w15 (gorge [] vs xmage [ability:Grand Nagus Zek@p0] @ step 20 (pass)); TRK-s430-rand xe:RAND:0:19:w11 (gorge [] vs xmage [ability:Grand Nagus Zek@p1] @ step 20 (pass)). Zek: 'Whenever another creature dies, create a Treasure token. This ability triggers only once each turn.' XMage puts a second Zek trigger on the stack at the pass where Zek dies together with another creature after it has already triggered that turn; gorge and Forge (the script's ActivationLimit$ 1) do not. CR 603.10a: leaves-the-battlefield abilities 'look back in time', so Zek does trigger for a creature that dies at the same time as it does, and CR 603.2 makes each such event trigger the one ability; the once-each-turn limit counts the triggerings of that same ability, and Zek leaving the battlefield does not make it a different ability, so a second triggering in the same turn is not allowed. Cause, read in XMage: TriggeredAbilityImpl.getKeyLastTurnTriggered / getKeyLastTurnTriggeredCount (Mage/src/main/java/mage/abilities/TriggeredAbilityImpl.java:82-93, read by updateTurnCount :105 and getRemainingTriggersLimitEachTurn :178) build the per-turn key with CardUtil.getCardZoneString(.., getSourceId(), game), which appends the card's CURRENT zone-change counter. When Zek and another creature die in one event Zek is already in the graveyard, its counter has moved, the key is new and the count reads 0, so the limit set by GrandNagusZek.java (.setTriggersLimitEachTurn(1)) does not hold. This is the cause already drafted in docs/upstream-bugs.md ('Issue text, Grand Nagus Zek'); that draft is now backed by a failing-first fork test. Failing-first GrandNagusZekTest.testDiesWithAnotherCreatureAfterTriggeringDoesNotTriggerAgain (the opponent's Lightning Bolt kills Grizzly Bears so Zek triggers once and is 2/2, then Fiery Cannonade kills Zek and Runeclaw Bear together; one Treasure expected): on the prebuilt mage 1.4.63 jars (xmageoracle-trek, ref 4142596) it fails '(Battlefield) Permanents counts for PlayerA are not equal (Treasure Token) expected:<1> but was:<2>', and passes with the patch, which keys the limit by the zone-change counter of the permanent the ability is on (game.getPermanentOrLKIBattlefield) while the ability is a battlefield ability; 8 existing once-each-turn test classes (TheEnigmaJewel, CuratorOfSunsCreation, ViviOrnitier, AmzuSwarmsHunger, PeterParker, SpiderVerse, BaronHelmutZemo, KambalProfiteeringMayor) pass 18/18 before and after. The ledger shows xmage:diverge:permanents=2 on this card as well (the second Treasure), the same mechanism's other face. evidence: blame|diverge|p0.life|Pitiless Fists. ECL four farm windows, all diverge p0.life with the GF|X three-way row (forge=agree): ECL-s280-rand xe:RAND:1:13:w18 step 19 (resolve) gorge 26 vs xmage 24; ECL-s393-rand xe:RAND:0:7:w12 step 6 (resolve) gorge 31 vs xmage 29; ECL-s399-rand xe:RAND:2:10:w8 step 16 (resolve) gorge 23 vs xmage 20; ECL-s421-rand xe:RAND:0:19:w9 step 15 (resolve) gorge 30 vs xmage 29. Verdict (b) XMage. The farm repro dirs are pruned (only REPRO.md and verdict.json were pulled), so the mechanism was measured by a one-scenario probe on this box instead. Pitiless Fists: 'When this Aura enters, enchanted creature fights up to one target creature an opponent controls.' with 'Enchanted creature gets +2/+2.' Probe (XMage build at XMAGE_REF 4142596, driver ScenarioReplay): p0 has Kinscaer Sentry (2/2 first strike, lifelink), casts Pitiless Fists on it (4/4) and picks p1's Grizzly Bears (2/2). Gorge p0.life 24 (the Sentry deals 4); XMage p0.life 22. Control: the same scenario against Craw Wurm (6/4) gives 24 in both (oraclediff diff AGREE), so the gain is capped at the target's remaining toughness only when the target is smaller than the damage; the 1, 2 and 3 life gaps in the four farm rows are the same cap (a lifelink creature enchanted by Fists fighting a creature with less toughness than its power). CR 701.14a: 'Each of those creatures deals damage equal to its power to the other creature.' CR 702.15b: 'Damage dealt by a source with lifelink causes that source's controller, or its owner if it has no controller, to gain that much life (in addition to any other results that damage causes).' So the enchanted 4/4 Sentry deals 4 damage to the Bears and p0 gains 4. CR 120.10 makes excess damage a bookkeeping amount ('excess damage equal to the difference was dealt'), the damage itself is not reduced. Cause, read in the pinned fork (079ae14f69): PermanentImpl.fightWithExcess (Mage/src/main/java/mage/game/permanent/PermanentImpl.java:2317) deals the fight damage with fightTarget.damageWithExcess(getPower().getValue(), getId(), source, game), and Permanent.damageWithExcess (Mage/src/main/java/mage/game/permanent/Permanent.java:220-226) computes 'int dealt = Math.min(lethal, damage); this.damage(dealt, attackerId, source, game);', i.e. it deals only the lethal amount and returns the rest as the excess figure. PermanentImpl.doDamage (PermanentImpl.java:1247-1253) then gains lifelink life from actualDamageDone, which is the capped amount (2), not the 4 the rules say. The line that should agree is Permanent.java:223-225: call this.damage(damage, attackerId, source, game) with the full amount and keep 'excess' as the separate return value. The same default method is the shared path for every damageWithExcess caller (DamageWithExcessEffect.java:52, RamThrough.java:88, WindswiftSlice.java:85, ContestOfClaws.java:70 and the one-sided excess burn spells), so it caps lifelink, damage-keyed triggers and damage replacement amounts for all of them. Forge and gorge both deal the full power (forge=agree). Fix: the same fork PR as the Plow Through rows. Pitiless Fists' fight reaches the cap through PermanentImpl.fightWithExcess, which fork PR #9 (adams-shaun/mage branch fix/damage-with-excess-full-damage 9385d741b3) rewrites to take the lethal amount first and then call fightTarget.damage(power, ...), so the fight and its lifelink gain are the whole power while the returned excess is unchanged. The change this row first proposed (Permanent.damageWithExcess dealing the full amount) is NOT the fix: that default is the 'excess damage is dealt to the controller instead' helper for DamageWithExcessEffect, Flame Spill and Ram Through, and dealing the full amount there deals the excess twice (the Plow Through seat measured it: Flame Spill control testFlameSpillExcessInsteadStillTruncated fails 'expected:<17> but was:<16>'); the other callers named above are left truncating on purpose. Boulder Dash: 'deals 2 damage to any target and 1 damage to any other target'; CR 601.2c: 'The player announces their choice of an appropriate object or player for each target the spell requires.' The window's cast chose targets that never included p0's Emissary (gorge and Forge agree), so no damage is marked on it (CR 120.3e) and no lethal-damage SBA applies to it. XMage killed it because the driver handed Boulder Dash's second target the answer queued for a LATER step. Cause: oracle/xmageoracle/src/org/mage/test/oracle/ScenarioReplay.java chooseTarget (line 1435) withholds the later object's 'targetPlayer=' answers through hideLaterPlayerTargets and restores them with getTargets().addAll(laterPlayers) (line 1439), which APPENDS them after every answer the window queued up front instead of putting them back where they were. With the queue [p1 creature, targetPlayer=PlayerB, <a later step's creature answer>], the first ask takes the creature, the player answer is restored behind the later step's answer, and the second ask then sees a non-player answer at the queue front with the player answer after it, so hideLaterPlayerTargets withholds that player answer as 'a later target object's' and TestPlayer.chooseTarget matches the later step's creature answer by name against the 'any other target' candidates and takes p0's own Emissary (1 damage kills a 1/1), leaving '[targetPlayer=PlayerB]' queued. That leftover is the stop signature of the six sibling xmage:diverge:p1.life Boulder Dash windows, attributed by the same stop and not replayed (ECL-s202-rand xe:RAND:0:12:w19, s265 xe:RAND:0:5:w11, s317 xe:RAND:4:19:w10, s335 xe:RAND:1:14:w10, s370 xe:RAND:3:2:w14, s377 xe:RAND:2:12:w11: 'Targets list was setup by addTarget with [targetPlayer=PlayerB], but not used' at an Equip ask, p1 one life higher in XMage because the 1 damage went to a creature). The windows' repro directories were pruned from the farm box, so the mechanism is proved on a constructed scenario, not a replay: p0 holds Virulent Emissary and Barbed Bloodletter, p1 holds Virulent Emissary; p0 casts Boulder Dash at [p1:Virulent Emissary, p1] and then equips p0:Virulent Emissary. CR 701.14a: 'a spell or ability may instruct two creatures to fight each other. When two creatures fight each other, each deals damage equal to its power to the other.' CR 702.15b: 'Damage dealt by a source with lifelink causes that source's controller ... to gain that much life.' A lifelink fighter must therefore gain its whole power. XMage gains only the lethal part: PermanentImpl.fightWithExcess (Mage/src/main/java/mage/game/permanent/PermanentImpl.java:2317) borrows Permanent.damageWithExcess(power, ...) for the fight (the helper is right for its 'excess instead' callers, wrong for a fight), whose default body (Mage/src/main/java/mage/game/permanent/Permanent.java:220-226) computes dealt = Math.min(lethal, damage) and calls this.damage(dealt, ...), so the damage and the lifelink gain are cut to getLethalDamage (1 when the damage source has deathtouch, else toughness minus damage already marked). Measured with a hand scenario (scenarios/oracle/spell-conditional/plow-through.json): Vampire Nighthawk (2/3 deathtouch lifelink) fights Craw Wurm: gorge p0 life 22, XMage 21; Baneslayer Angel (5 power, lifelink) fights Llanowar Elves: gorge 25, XMage 21. Both scenarios pass on gorge in TestOracleAudit (make test-one PKG=./audit RUN='^TestOracleAudit$/Plow_Through'). Fix on the fork: adams-shaun/mage branch fix/damage-with-excess-full-damage (9385d741b3), PR #9. Permanent.damageWithExcess is left truncating on purpose: its other callers implement 'excess damage is dealt to that creature's controller instead' (DamageWithExcessEffect, Flame Spill, Ram Through with trample) and would deal the excess twice if it dealt the full amount. The defect is only the fight path, so PermanentImpl.fightWithExcess no longer borrows the helper: it takes the lethal damage before the damage, computes excess = max(power - lethal, 0), then calls fightTarget.damage(power, ...), so the fight deals the whole power and still returns the excess its callers measure (The Last Agni Kai, Rhino's Rampage, Ezuri's Predation). Fork tests (Mage.Tests org.mage.test.cards.single.dft.PlowThroughTest, run as JUnit on the prebuilt mage 1.4.63 jars at ref 4142596 because maven cannot run in the compliance seat; the fix class is PermanentImpl compiled from the ref's source with the same edit and put ahead of the jar): testLifelinkDeathtouchFightGainsWholePower (Nighthawk vs Craw Wurm, expects p0 22) and testLifelinkFightGainsWholePowerNotToughness (Baneslayer vs Llanowar Elves, expects 25) fail before with 'expected:<22> but was:<21>' and 'expected:<25> but was:<21>' (the farm values) and pass after; the controls testFlameSpillExcessInsteadStillTruncated (Flame Spill 4 at Boros Reckoner 3/3: the Reckoner is dealt 3 and reflects 3, so p0 17, controller 19) and testFlameSpillOnBears (2 to the Bears' controller) pass before and after, and ExcessDamageTest (8 tests) passes before and after.
